author: AR Content Designer
objectives: Students will identify and name the four chambers of the heart, the four heart valves, and the major vessels entering and leaving the heart.
Students will trace the path of blood through the heart's dual circulation, naming each chamber, valve, and vessel in order.
Students will distinguish the pulmonary circuit from the systemic circuit and explain why the right and left sides of the heart serve different circulatory functions.

Students will explain why the left ventricle has a substantially thicker myocardium than the right ventricle, relating wall thickness to the pressure required to perfuse the systemic versus pulmonary circuits.
Students will describe the function of the atrioventricular and semilunar valves in preventing backflow, and identify which valves separate which chambers or chamber-vessel pairs.

modules.description: Introduction to the external and internal gross anatomy of the human heart, including its anatomical orientation.
modules.author: AR Content Designer
educationalObjectives: Identify the anatomical orientation of the heart within the human body.
Differentiate between the external surface and internal cutaway views of the heart.

modules.description: A step-by-step tour identifying the four chambers, four valves, and major vessels of the heart.
modules.author: AR Content Designer
educationalObjectives: Identify and name the four chambers of the heart (right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle).
Identify and name the four heart valves (tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral/bicuspid, aortic).
Identify and name the major vessels entering and leaving the heart (superior/inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries/veins, aorta).

modules.description: Visualize the flow of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through the heart's pulmonary and systemic circuits.
modules.author: AR Content Designer
educationalObjectives: Distinguish the pulmonary circuit from the systemic circuit.
Explain how the right and left sides of the heart serve different circulatory functions (deoxygenated vs. oxygenated blood).

modules.description: Follow a single red blood cell through the entire dual circulatory pathway.
modules.author: AR Content Designer
educationalObjectives: Trace the complete path of a red blood cell through the pulmonary and systemic circuits.
Identify changes in blood oxygenation status as blood moves through different organs.

modules.description: Examine the difference in myocardial wall thickness between the right and left ventricles and its functional significance.
modules.author: AR Content Designer
educationalObjectives: Explain why the left ventricle has a thicker myocardium than the right ventricle.
Relate ventricular wall thickness to the pressure required for systemic versus pulmonary circulation.

modules.description: Explore the structure and function of the heart's four valves in preventing blood backflow.
modules.author: AR Content Designer
educationalObjectives: Describe the function of atrioventricular (tricuspid and mitral) and semilunar (pulmonary and aortic) valves.
Identify when each valve is open or closed during the cardiac cycle to prevent backflow.

components.text: Ventricular Contraction: AV Valves Closed, Semilunar Valves Open
Ventricular Relaxation: AV Valves Open, Semilunar Valves Closed

modules.description: Test your knowledge by identifying key heart structures.
modules.author: AR Content Designer
educationalObjectives: Accurately identify and name the four chambers, four valves, and major vessels of the heart.

modules.description: Test your understanding of the blood flow path through the heart and circulatory system.
modules.author: AR Content Designer
educationalObjectives: Accurately sequence the path of blood through all major heart chambers, valves, and vessels.
Correctly identify the next structure in the blood flow pathway.
